newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Powerful car bomb discovered in southwest Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Powerful car bomb discovered in southwest Colombia.

text.p: A powerful car bomb was discovered early on Tuesday in Colombia's second largest city and police said it was the work of drug lords opposed to lifting the country's constitutional ban on extradition.

"This definitely has to be the work of drug traffickers," National Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano said of the bomb, which consisted of about 360 pounds (163 kg) of dynamite and was discovered at 3:28 a.m. (8:28 GMT) in the centre of the southwest city of Cali.

"This should serve as a warning to all Colombians," Serrano added, saying it was possible that drug traffickers opposed to extradition were planning to unleash a wave of "narco-violence and narco-terrorism" like the one that swept across Colombia in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
Extradition was banned by Congress in 1991, in a bid to end the campaign of terror waged by traffickers like Pablo Escobar, the late and notoriously violent leader of the Medellin drug cartel.

A Senate judicial panel recently approved legislation that would lift the ban, however, and Justice Minister Carlos Medellin told reporters last week that drug kingpins already serving time in Colombian jails might soon face the prospect of being tried in foreign courts.
The legislation that would remove the ban on extradition was scheduled for debate by the Senate on Tuesday afternoon.

"Extradition and asset forfeiture is what hurts drug traffickers the most," Serrano said, referring to a separate bill pending before Congress that would allow the government to seize the property of reputed billionaires like Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela, the jailed leaders of the Cali drug mob.
Serrano, who spoke in an interview with the Caracol radio network, said an anonymous telephone caller led police to the Cali bomb.

He did not elaborate, but a police spokeswoman in Cali said the explosive device was stashed in a white mini-bus that had been reported stolen 15 days ago. It was parked outside a chemical plant belonging to the family of Senastor Claudia Blum, one of the sponsors of the bill that would lift the ban on extradition.

The bomb was connected to the vehicle's battery and set to detonate whenever the ignition was turned on, the spokeswoman said. She said it was not immediately clear if there was any link between the device and two small bombs detonated on Monday night outside a police academy in northeastern Cali. The bombs caused minor roperty damage but no injuries.
